advisories.query: early blight potato India management advisory
advisories.answer: To manage early blight in potato crops in India, sources recommend using fungicides, particularly systemic fungicides that inhibit pathogen growth after infection. Organic growers are limited to protectant fungicides like copper-based fungicides and Bacillus subtilis biofungicides. Cultural practices such as planting resistant varieties, crop rotation with non-host crops, balanced nitrogen fertilization, and avoiding excessive irrigation are also advised. Fungicide applications should be timed based on disease risk, with early and frequent applications in high-risk regions and less frequent applications in lower-risk areas. Good resistance management strategies include rotating fungicides with differing modes of action and using multisite fungicides.

results.title: How To Manage Early Blight in Your Potato Crops - Growing Produce
results.content:
Organic potato growers are limited to protectant fungicides, including copper-based fungicides and Bacillus subtilis biofungicides, for early blight management. When these are the only options, starting early and repeating at shorter intervals is generally advised.

Systemic fungicides are absorbed into plant tissues and can inhibit pathogen growth after infection. They are most effective when applied within hours or a few days of infection. results.title: Early Blight of Potato | NDSU Agriculture
results.content:
Most commercially acceptable potato cultivars are susceptible to early blight; therefore, foliar fungicide application is the primary means for managing early blight.
 Fungicide selection and rotation should be approached with the goals of obtaining effective disease management and reducing the risk of the early blight pathogen developing fungicide insensitivity.
 Practice good resistance management strategies by 1) rotating and combining (tank-mix or prepackaged) fungicides with differing modes of action and 2) including multisite (group M) fungicides.

proposal.headline: No drone flight recommended; all zones need human review before any action.
proposal.rationale: Inspection found early blight in zones A2 and B2 (severity 2, confidence 0.65 and 0.6) while other zones appeared healthy. Simulation showed that a drone spot‑spray of protectant fungicide would raise the worst‑20% margin by INR 2365/ha and be better than no action in 100% of simulated seasons for those zones. However every zone is flagged for human review because the vision model’s conformal set is empty (uncalibrated, p>=0.85 gate), so the drone cannot treat any zone until a human verifies the findings. Therefore no flight is proposed at this time.
